text:
marie: Heads-up — after last night's kernel+driver push (kernel 6.6.12 + NVIDIA driver 540.12) we're seeing NCCl/NVLink peering failures on a subset of mixed H100/A100 racks in us-west2. Some jobs fell back to SHM and then NET/socket and latency spiked.

sam: ugh. which nodes specifically? have we correlated SKU or driver microbuilds?

marie: nodes with mixed H100/A100 (rack-uw2-gpu-1{2,3,4}) — logs show nvlink peer discovery timeouts on the H100 side. A100-only racks look fine.

liam: paste the relevant logs? quick grep output helps.

marie: here's the core probe output from one affected host:
```
[  120.412345] nvlink peer query failed: -110
[  120.412348] nvlink: nvlink_probe: peer timeout for p2p discovery
[  120.412350] nvidia: NVLINK: link status mismatch, skipping nvlink attach
```

julia: also seeing NCCL warnings in the pod logs:
```
NCCL WARN NET/Socket : no usable p2p, falling back to socket
NCCL INFO Using coll net/socket for rank 0
```

sre-oncall: what's the distribution of failures? just us-west2? any correlation with kernel patch level or node image?

marie: so far only us-west2 racks that were upgraded last night (image: redwood-gpu-2026-06-14). us-east and eu clusters untouched yet.

sam: can we repro with `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` and `dmesg` on an affected host? also check `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`.

marie: ran those. topo matrix shows NVLink links missing between H100 and A100 on the same host. `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` output snippet:
```
GPU0 GPU1 CPU
GPU0  X   SYS  PHB
GPU1 SYS   X   PHB
```
(should show NVLINK for H100<->H100 pairs, but H100<->A100 missing)

liam: that suggests a probe/enumeration regression in the kernel-driver interaction for hetero pairs. Might be due to new kernel using different PCI ordering, or a driver small change.

julia: are any pods/queues in Dedicated/reserved capacity impacted? We need to know customer visible impact.

marie: a few internal inference jobs on dedicated pools saw 2-3x latency and OOM spikes due to increased CPU copy overhead. No customer SLA breaches yet, but it's close for some heavy-throughput tenants.

sre-oncall: action items: 1) isolate affected hosts from orchestrator to avoid new scheduling 2) rollback drivers on a canary host 3) open NVIDIA SR and attach logs 4) add autoscale buffer for capacity.

sam: started a job to mark rack-uw2-gpu-123 and 124 cordoned (k8s) and drain; I'll keep 2 nodes for debug. Also creating a rollback image using driver 535.86. 540.12 might be culprit.

marie: rollback plan SGTM. We should also run `modinfo nvidia` and compare kernel symbols across kernels; I've recorded the `dmesg` traces and PCI ids.

liam: quick check — are we seeing consistent kernel taint or PCIe AER errors? `dmesg | grep -i aer`?

marie: grep shows some AER entries but sparse. primary pattern is NVLINK peer probe timeouts. I'll attach full logs to the ticket.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1927 "NVLink peering failures after kernel+driver upgrade (us-west2)" — assigned to eng-infra oncall.

sre-oncall: thanks infra-bot. Sam, prioritize rollback on 2 debug nodes and run a controlled job to confirm NVLink restored. Marie, collect `nvidia-persistenced` logs and `lspci -vvv` for those hosts.

sam: rolled driver back on rack-uw2-gpu-123 (to driver 535.86) and rebooted. nvlink topo now shows expected links on that host. Running a microbench + NCCL all-reduce.

marie: nice — microbench shows `ncclAllReduce` latency back to baseline on the rolled host. The still-upgraded hosts remain in socket fallback.

julia: we need a short customer note for any tenants hitting higher latency — marketing/growth will craft messaging. Also, we should consider a hold on kernel/driver upgrades until we validate on hetero racks.

liam: long-term: add a preflight test that exercises hetero NVLink pairs and NCCL peering during image bake. Short-term: blacklist driver 540.12 for mixed racks.

sre-oncall: agreeing. I'll add a rollout freeze for mixed-sku pools and create a scheduler rule to prefer homogeneous racks for now.

marie: FYI cost impact: socket fallback increases cross-host traffic and CPU overhead — we estimate ~15-25% extra infra cost for affected tenants if prolonged. Will track in the incident doc.

infra-bot: Updated #INC-2026-1927 with logs and mitigation steps. NVIDIA SR #SR-998271 opened.

sam: plan to fully rollback the rest of the upgraded us-west2 racks tonight (maintenance window 02:00 UTC) unless NVIDIA provides a hotfix.

julia: thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread and paste perf numbers after each rollback. :thumbsup:

marie: will do, starting post-rollback validation now.

sre-oncall: closing loop only after we see 24h stability on the rolled nodes or a vendor patch.
